overview.about: Earth Day is the world's largest environmental observance, first held in 1970 and now mobilising around a billion people across nearly 200 countries. It has become a cornerstone of the modern environmental movement and a focal point for climate action.
overview.nextEvent: The next Earth Day is marked on 22 April with clean-ups, campaigns, education and climate events around the world. Each year adopts a global theme to focus attention and drive collective action.

@graph.name: Earth Day
@graph.description: Earth Day is held every 22 April and brings schools, civic groups, scientists and businesses into a shared public conversation about environmental protection. The first Earth Day in 1970 helped make environmental issues visible in American public life; it is now observed internationally. Its strength is breadth rather than one prescribed ritual: local organisers choose clean-ups, restoration work, public talks, climate education or policy campaigns that fit their place. A useful Earth Day plan starts with one local action and one question about the systems behind it, such as waste, energy, transport or habitat. That keeps the observance rooted in a specific community rather than turning it into a generic environmental slogan.

exploreIntro: These are not Earth Day host countries. They show three environments where the day?s local action becomes concrete: Australia?s coasts and reefs, Kenya?s wildlife landscapes, and Switzerland?s Alpine watersheds.
participationIntro: Pick one visible action rather than trying to do everything:

participationSteps.text: Join a cleanup, planting, repair, reuse or climate-awareness activity if one is available nearby.
Use the day to make one household, school or workplace habit easier to keep after the day is over.
Share specific environmental information instead of vague slogans.
If organising something, make it practical: time, place, supplies and a clear action.
